## Purpose and execution
Fast Note Sync Service is a Go server for multi-device Obsidian vault synchronization, administration, REST automation, and MCP-based AI access. The executable starts at `main.go`; Cobra-style operational commands, including `run`, bootstrap, upgrade, password reset, and version, are under `cmd/root.go`, `cmd/run.go`, and `cmd/run_server.go`. Runtime assembly is centralized in `internal/app/app.go`.

## Composition root and configuration
Application startup loads configuration, initializes infrastructure, repositories, services, routers, and lifecycle/restart handling. Core wiring paths are `internal/app/config.go`, `internal/app/infra.go`, and `internal/app/services.go`. Configuration covers server, database, storage, security, OAuth/OIDC, Git, tracing, tunnel, and Web GUI concerns in `internal/config/`; the deployable default is `config/config.yaml`.

## HTTP/API and static-admin boundary
The server exposes REST endpoints, health/metrics, versioning, administration, vault/note/file/folder management, sharing, backups, Git sync, and authentication through `internal/routers/router.go` and `internal/routers/api_router/handler.go`. Middleware applies recovery, access logging, CORS/proxy behavior, request limits, tracing, language, and separate user/WebGUI/share/MCP auth boundaries in `internal/middleware/`. Prebuilt React admin assets are served from `frontend/index.html` and `frontend/assets/`.

## Real-time sync pipeline
WebSocket is the primary bidirectional synchronization transport for clients. `internal/routers/router_websocket.go` mounts the protocol; `internal/routers/websocket_router/handler.go` dispatches actions for notes, files, folders, and settings. Its sync pipeline includes batch/download caches and conflict notification paths such as `internal/routers/websocket_router/ws_sync_batch_cache.go` and `internal/routers/websocket_router/ws_note.go`. Protobuf sync schema and generated bindings reside at `internal/proto/v1/sync.proto` and `internal/proto/v1/sync.pb.go`.

## Domain, persistence, and mutation services
Domain entities represent vaults, notes/history/links/full-text search, folders/files, users/tokens/OIDC identities, sharing, storage, backup, Git sync, and sync logs under `internal/domain/`. GORM-generated models/queries and repository implementations separate database access from business rules: `internal/model/model.go`, `internal/query/gen.go`, `internal/dao/dao.go`. Services coordinate CRUD, conflict handling, history, sharing, authentication, storage, backup, and Git-driven side effects, notably `internal/service/note_service.go`, `internal/service/conflict_service.go`, and `internal/service/vault_service.go`.

## MCP and identity integrations
MCP exposes note, folder, file, and vault tools over Streamable HTTP and SSE, routed through `internal/routers/router_mcp.go` and implemented in `internal/routers/mcp_router/mcp.go`. Tool mutations use the same service layer, allowing WebSocket propagation to connected sync clients. Token authentication is supported; optional Stytch OAuth verification/mapping is in `internal/oauth/verifier.go` and `internal/oauth/stytch_client.go`. Web GUI OIDC provider/state and service integration are in `internal/oidc/provider.go` and `internal/service/oidc_service.go`.

## Background operations and infrastructure
A task manager/scheduler runs backup, version checks, database cleanup, temporary-file cleanup, note-history retention, sync maintenance, and support-data updates: `internal/task/manager.go`, `internal/task/scheduler.go`, `internal/task/task_backup.go`. Backups and one-way mirrors target local FS, S3-compatible services, Aliyun OSS, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, or WebDAV via `pkg/storage/storage.go`. Deployment supports native binaries and Docker through `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/docker-compose.yaml`, and `docker/entrypoint.sh`; supported relational databases are SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL.
